Follow `RULES.md` strictly for coding quality, validation, lint budgets, and definition of done. `WORKFLOW.md` governs issues, branches, PRs, reviews, and merges; `RELEASING.md` governs releases. Repo tooling and explicit user instructions override this file.

For concrete requests, start with relevant files; otherwise inspect top-level docs, manifests, and module READMEs. Do not assume module scope. Read every file fully before editing. Preserve intentional functionality; fix dependency/type problems at their source. Keep diffs tight and protect other agents’ changes. Resolve conflicts only in files you changed; if untouched files conflict, stop and ask.

After code changes, run repository validation commands. Treat formatter, lint, warnings-as-errors, tests, and coverage as design constraints. Do not bypass hooks, checks, or validation steps.
Never use `--no-verify`.
Never commit unless the user explicitly asks. If committing, commit only files changed in this session; use explicit paths; run `git status` and verify staged files. Include `fixes #<number>` or `closes #<number>` when related.
`git add <specific-file-paths>`
`git pull --rebase`
`git reset --hard`
`git clean -fd`
`git commit --no-verify`

Read full issues, including comments. Analyze PRs before local changes. Do not open PRs, merge, or close unless explicitly asked.

Keep responses concise, direct, and technical. No emojis in commits, issues, PR comments, or code comments unless asked.

Store transient state under `.llm/{DIR}/`, choosing `{DIR}` to avoid collisions. Do not use `.context/`; treat `.llm/` as disposable, untracked state. Promote durable context to tracked docs.
